title: Senate Combo: Ohio and Texas
description:
This market will resolve according to the outcome of the United States Senate general elections in Ohio and Texas (including the special election in Ohio) that are currently scheduled for November 3, 2026, inclusive of any potential runoffs. 

A candidate will be considered to represent a party by their ballot-listed affiliation or if they are the nominee of that party. Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

If the results of one of these elections are not conclusively known by March 31, 2027, or if an independent or third-party candidate wins one of these elections, this market will resolve to "Other". 

For purposes of this market, a "sweep" is when a party wins all races. 

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources have conclusively called the relevant elections. If all three sources do not achieve consensus in calling the relevant races for this market, it will resolve based on the official certification.

title: Senate Combo: Louisiana, Mississippi, Florida
description:
This market will resolve according to the outcome of the United States Senate general elections in Louisiana, Mississippi, and Florida that are currently scheduled for November 3, 2026, inclusive of any potential runoffs. 

A candidate will be considered to represent a party by their ballot-listed affiliation or if they are the nominee of that party. Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

If the results of one of these elections are not conclusively known by March 31, 2027, or if an independent or third-party candidate wins one of these elections, this market will resolve to "Other". 

For purposes of this market, a "sweep" is when a party wins all races. 

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources have conclusively called the relevant elections. If all three sources do not achieve consensus in calling the relevant races for this market, it will resolve based on the official certification.

title: Alaska Senate loser concedes by...?
description:

Only public statements from the relevant candidate will qualify. Reports of private conversations (e.g., if the candidate called the victor and conceded over the phone) will not count.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

title: Governor Combo: Vermont and New Hampshire
description:
This market will resolve according to the outcome of the gubernatorial general elections in Vermont and New Hampshire that are currently scheduled for November 3, 2026, inclusive of any potential runoffs or other procedures used to determine the winner. 

A candidate will be considered to represent a party by their ballot-listed affiliation or if they are the nominee of that party. Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

If the results of one of these elections are not conclusively known by March 31, 2027, or if an independent or third-party candidate wins one of these elections, this market will resolve to "Other". 

For purposes of this market, a "sweep" is when a party wins both races. 

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources have conclusively called the relevant elections. If all three sources do not achieve consensus in calling the relevant races for this market, it will resolve based on the official certification.

title: Senate MOV Ranking: Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Alaska
description:
The 2026 midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the order of the margins of victory in the 2026 United States Senate elections in Texas, Ohio (special election), Kansas, and Alaska, ranked from lowest (closest) to highest.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the relevant round of the election.

For elections that include runoffs, ranked-choice, or other multi-round elections, the relevant margin of victory will be that of the round in which the winner is determined.

If two or more of these states have identical margins of victory, the tie will be broken alphabetically by state name, with the state that comes first alphabetically treated as having the smaller margin of victory.

This market will resolve based on the official vote counts once the counts have been made official.

If a recount is initiated before any applicable vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the results of one of these elections are not conclusively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a compilation of all of the relevant state election authorities responsible for certifying statewide elections, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. title: Will Republicans lose any "Solid / Likely R" House race?
description:

The winner of each race is determined including any runoff or other relevant procedure under the applicable rules of the relevant jurisdiction.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their office, after election day, the seat is attributed to the party under which the person was elected.

In the event that the winner of an election cannot be determined by March 31, 2027, that election will not be considered for purposes of this market. 

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.
